transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-23
Time: 15:30 - 16:16 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Ava Moreno (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Liu Chen (Redwood SE), Jenna Torres (Clearline VP Eng), Marcus Lee (Infra Lead), Priya Nair (Product), Diego Alvarez (Security)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be partial): customer evaluating Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private for inference. Main concerns: burst readiness, tenant isolation, prewarming, KMS/SOC2 for PHI-like data, cost/latency tradeoffs. Agreed next steps: run synthetic peak test, share security docs, exchange sample prompts and traffic profiles.

Transcript:
[00:00] Ava: Okay hi everyone thanks for joining, this is Ava from Redwood, i'm the AE on this account. we've got Samir and Liu from solutions. how's everyone doing?
[00:10] Jenna: Hi thanks, good to be here. we want to focus on dedicated capacity — we have fairly spiky traffic and some data residency requirements
[00:18] Marcus: yeah we saw your hosted latency numbers but we're worried about multi-tenant noisy neighbor effects during our end-of-month spikes
[00:25] Samir: totally makes sense. quick question up front — are you leaning dedicated reserved capacity, or private VPC/onprem?
[00:32] Jenna: leaning dedicated reserved, because we want predictable throughput and less ops overhead than full onprem. but we want isolation guarantees.
[00:40] Diego: and we need KMS integration and audit logs — SOC 2 stuff. also encryption in transit/rest at rest — usual checklist.
[00:48] Liu: we can integrate with customer-managed KMS for Private and Dedicated, and the control plane audit logs are available for Dedicated. we'll share the SOC2 artefacts after NDA.
[00:56] Priya: on the burst profile — our product has a core steady state of about 200 rps but on certain events it spikes to 3k for 8-12 minutes, and then falls back. we need to understand prewarm and burst capacity options.
[01:12] Samir: helpful — that spike shape is exactly the kind of thing our warm-pool + burst routing is built for. couple followups: what model family are you using and approximate token sizes?
[01:22] Jenna: we're testing an open Llama-derivative for generation at ~1k tokens on average, some flows push to 4k. quantization is in our roadmap but for quality reasons we're starting 16-bit.
[01:34] Marcus: and we have a soft SLA of p95 < 350ms for user-facing single-turn generation, and p99 under 1.2s. is that realistic on dedicated?
[01:44] Samir: depends on model and GPU profile, but on Dedicated reserved pools we get close — our measurements show p95 in the 200-400ms range for trimmed 1k prompts on A100-style nodes when prewarmed. p99 can be higher with cold caches. the KV cache and prefix caching helps a lot for conversational workloads.
[02:00] Jenna: when you say prewarmed, how fast is warm-pool spin-up and what's the cost impact?
[02:06] Liu: warm pools keep a subset of workers ready, prewarmed instances can be allocated in tens of seconds. cost is a mix — reserved capacity commits rental of GPUs, warm-pool is a fraction of that cost to keep GPUs in hot state. we can show a pricing sketch.
[02:20] Priya: one of our constraints is an overall monthly budget cap; we can't just double infra spend for burst. we need to model cost-per-peak-minute.
[02:28] Ava: understood — we'll run a synthetic peak run using your traffic histogram and show cost delta for warm pools vs on-demand burst. we'll also include an alternative: intelligent batching + prefix caching which can reduce token cost.
[02:41] Marcus: what's the path if dedicated capacity is saturated? fallback to hosted variants?
[02:46] Samir: yes, we have routing fallbacks. you can set policies: prefer dedicated, fallback to a lower-cost hosted model or a smaller quantized variant. we can model quality degradation tradeoffs.
[02:57] Diego: that raises data governance issues — if fallback goes to hosted, does data leave our VPC or get logged by Redwood?
[03:03] Liu: good point. fallbacks can be constrained — we can route only anonymized requests or only non-PII traffic to hosted. for strict data residency we recommend Private deployment. we'll document the routing guarantees.
[03:15] Jenna: on isolation — we need to ensure noisy neighbor risk is mitigated. is dedicated a single-tenant GPU pool or multi-tenant with isolation primitives?
[03:22] Samir: Dedicated uses reserved GPU pools that are tenant-isolated at the node level; you don't share the same worker processes with other customers. there are degrees of isolation (node fencing, tenant sharding) — we can size a pool to minimize cross-tenant interference.
[03:35] Marcus: and preemption? what if cloud provider preempts GPU instances — how does Redwood handle that?
[03:40] Liu: we have eviction handlers and we provision spare capacity for SLA tiers; if using Dedicated with our burst pool, we can provide evict-protected nodes for critical workloads. also cross-region fallback is an option.
[03:52] Jenna: excellent. are there any benchmark artifacts you can run against our real prompt set?
[03:57] Samir: yes — we usually run synthetic peak tests and an eval harness. if you share a representative prompt corpus and traffic histogram, we'll run a 1-hour synthetic peak with your 50-150 concurrent user pattern and capture p50/p95/p99 and token cost.
[04:12] Priya: timeline wise we're aiming for a pilot in early January; selection decision by mid-December. is that doable?
[04:19] Ava: yes, that's doable. next step would be the benchmark run before Thanksgiving US — or realistically we can do the bench by 11/30 and a results review in first week of December.
[04:29] Marcus: security: Diego will need a KMS integration diagram, key rotation policy, and audit log retention details.
[04:36] Diego: also SSO/SCIM for RBAC and separation of roles — we need to verify identity provider compatibility.
[04:43] Liu: we support SAML and OIDC, SCIM provisioning for groups, RBAC scoping at model/route level, and will include our audit log schema.
[04:51] Jenna: a practical question: how do you handle KV cache warm-up across many short-lived requests? our users do a lot of completions that share prefixes.
[04:59] Samir: prefix caching and KV cache are managed by the runtime — for highly-shared prefixes we can maintain warmed KV fragments, plus continuous batching within a window to coalesce requests. there are knobs for TTLs and cache size per pool.
[05:13] Priya: any gotchas with large prompts reaching 4k tokens?
[05:17] Liu: sequence length impacts memory and kernel selection; beyond ~2k you might see throughput drop unless using partitioned KV or model variants. quantization and compiled kernels help but you need to test with your prompt set.
[05:29] Marcus: can we run tests in our VPC (private) or do we need to send prompts over the internet?
[05:34] Ava: two options: Dedicated with VPC peering (control plane is still managed) or Private where the control plane can be customer-run. for bench tests we can run a dedicated pool in our test region and route traffic through secure peering.
[05:47] Diego: and if we do Private, what's the ops burden? we have a small infra team.
[05:51] Samir: Private requires more ops: hardware, networking, and potentially an onprem package. Dedicated hits middle ground — low customer ops, but full isolation at node level. we'll outline tradeoffs in a one-pager.
[06:05] Jenna: let's talk numbers — what would an 8-GPU reserved pool look like in cost ballpark and what warm-pool sizing would you suggest for our spike profile?
[06:14] Ava: we'll provide a pricing sketch, but ballpark: dedicated pool pricing varies by GPU type and region; warm-pools are typically sized 10-25% of peak concurrency for fast prewarm. exact numbers after synthetic run.
[06:25] Marcus: curious about model variants — could we use a quantized variant for background batch jobs and full float for interactive?
[06:30] Liu: absolutely — routing policies can send lower-priority or background requests to quantized/cheaper variants while preserving full precision for interactive routes.
[06:38] Priya: any points on monitoring and cost observability? we need per-route cost and token-level breakdowns, ideally actionable alerts when per-token cost deviates.
[06:47] Samir: Redwood Console shows per-route token breakdown, traces and a cost drilldown, plus alerts. we can send screenshots and a demo recording.
[06:56] Jenna: what about model rollouts? we want canary and A/B to safeguard quality during quantized rollouts.
[07:01] Liu: rollouts are supported with traffic splitting and auto rollback on quality regressions tied to your eval prompts.
[07:08] Diego: anything specifically about compliance for PHI? we handle regulated data in our product; Do you have experience with HIPAA-like controls?
[07:16] Samir: while we don't offer a HIPAA-certified hosted service by default, Dedicated + Private deployments with customer-managed keys and isolated networks can be architected to meet HIPAA constraints. we'd need legal and security sign-off; we can share references from similar customers.
[07:32] Jenna: can you share any artifacts that show performance variance during spikes (like a 3k rps 10-minute window)?
[07:38] Ava: yes — Samir will run a synthetic peak and include a short report with p50/p95/p99 and cost per peak-minute and per-token.
[07:46] Marcus: one more technical — what about preemption during scaling events? do you hold spare hot slots?
[07:52] Liu: for higher SLAs we keep warm-protected nodes and pre-allocated burst capacity; the behavior is configurable by contract tier.
[08:01] Priya: can you simulate our exact burst cadence? sometimes it's a sawtooth — three spikes over 30 minutes.
[08:07] Samir: yes we'll simulate the sawtooth and also do a sustained flat spike to compare. we'll capture eviction rates and tail latencies.
[08:16] Jenna: ok good. what's the minimum commit period for Dedicated?
[08:19] Ava: typically monthly or annual reserved capacity; we can do a pilot month with a smaller commitment and convert to annual if you opt in.
[08:26] Diego: concerning keys — can Redwood rotate KMS keys automatically or do we require manual rotation?
[08:31] Liu: we support both patterns; customer-managed keys can be rotated with limited disruption if you follow recommended patterns. we'll include a rotation playbook.
[08:43] Priya: are there known pitfalls when third-party telemetry injects additional latency? we integrate with a tracing sidecar.
[08:49] Samir: tracing sidecars can add overhead; we recommend sampling strategies and offloading some telemetry to asynchronous pipelines. we can show config examples.
[08:58] Jenna: anything about data retention — logs and prompt retention windows?
[09:02] Liu: retention is configurable; for Dedicated you can opt shorter retention or forward logs to your S3. audit logs for compliance are stored according to contract.
[09:12] Ava: we're nearly halfway — do we want to pivot to concrete test plan now?
[09:16] Jenna: yes please. outline what you need from us.
[09:20] Samir: we'll need: sample prompt corpus, traffic histogram (minute granularity preferred), desired SLA targets, list of routes that are interactive vs background, and a security contact for KMS questions.
[09:31] Jenna: we'll send the corpus and histogram. Marcus will own the infra files, Diego will own security.
[09:36] Priya: timeline reiteration: bench by 11/30, results review first week of Dec, pilot in Jan.
[09:43] Ava: sounds good. recap and deliverables: Samir synthetic bench + report; Ava pricing sketch and security docs; Liu caching and ops notes.
[09:52] Marcus: do you have any restriction on model artifacts? we have some licensed models — need guidance for licensing in Dedicated/Private.
[09:58] Liu: model licensing depends on your license terms; we can host customer models in Dedicated or Private as long as the license permits. we'll share best practices.
[10:08] Jenna: cost sensitivity again — can warm-pool be autoscaled down quickly after spike? we don't want long tail charges.
[10:13] Samir: warm pools scale down with configurable cooldowns; you can tune to avoid paying for long tails but faster cooldowns risk cache coldness. tradeoff.
[10:23] Priya: is there a cost model for prefix caching efficiency improvements? any rough % improvement numbers?
[10:28] Samir: depends on overlap; for heavy prefix reuse we often see 15-40% token cost reduction, sometimes more if reuse is extreme.
[10:37] Diego: final security Q: does Redwood support HSM-backed keys for the most sensitive configs?
[10:42] Liu: yes HSM-backed KMS is supported for Private and enterprise Dedicated arrangements.
[10:48] Ava: OK wrapping up — are there any outstanding blockers?
[10:52] Jenna: none from product. security will follow up but not a blocker. pricing caveat is internal but not a showstopper.
[10:59] Ava: excellent. we'll send the materials and run the bench. thanks everyone.
[11:04] Samir: thanks all.
[11:06] Diego: thanks.

End of transcript.
